info.name: Bachs Checkout (unofficial SDK)
info.description:
Generated from the official Bachs OpenAPI spec (spec/bachs-openapi.json), plus a curated SDK Flow folder.

**Auth:** collection-level Bearer {{BACHS_SECRET_KEY}}. Pick an environment (Sandbox / Live) - the key and baseUrl swap together, nothing else changes.

**Money:** always a decimal string at currency precision, paired with an ISO 4217 code. Never minor units.

**Idempotency:** the collection pre-request script attaches an Idempotency-Key to every POST/PATCH automatically, as the API requires.

**Truth:** fulfilment comes from the collection.succeeded webhook, never from the browser or from a 201 response.

item.name: SDK Flow: create the payment
item.description: Server side, secret key. Creates the catalog item and the checkout session, then reads the settled money back. Nothing here touches a customer's browser.

request.description: A checkout session always prices off a product. Skip if you already have {{product_id}}.

item.name: 2. Create checkout session  ->  the payment request

request.description:
Server-side only, secret key. Returns checkout_url + client_secret. The token segment of checkout_url is the credential for every call in the next folder - it needs no API key, which is why your browser can drive the checkout without seeing your secret.

Optional: add "payment_method_types": ["USD_CARD", "NGN_CARD"] to restrict the rails offered - note it is enforced server-side, so a rail you exclude returns PAYMENT_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED later.

item.name: 2b. Create checkout session - RAW AMOUNT (no product)

request.description: Product-less session: `pricing` replaces `product_cart` and they are mutually exclusive. The detail response then carries `products: null` and the amount you set here is the amount charged. Minimums apply for some currencies (NGN needs at least 100.00).

item.name: 2c. Create checkout session - BUYER-CHOSEN amount (custom pricing)

request.description: Pay-what-you-want, still product-less. The buyer picks the amount within your bounds; you can also set it server-side with the set-amount call in the next folder.
Amount 0.00 and `payment_required: false`. Completing it returns payment_type=redirect with a payment_url, and the session lands on completed - useful for trials and comped access.

item.name: 2e. Create checkout session - CATALOG with per-line price override

request.description: Middle ground: keep the catalog product, override the price for this one session. The catalog is untouched and the override is never added to the price list.
Full session object once the customer has paid: charge, fees, customer_details.

query.description: succeeded | failed | pending

request.description: What actually settled, with fees and refunds. Filter by reference/status/date.
No page, no customer present: needs a card already saved at a previous checkout (save_payment_method: true). Always returns a payment - a refusal is in status, not an error.
Refunds settle asynchronously; refund.paid confirms delivery.

item.name: Custom UI: drive the checkout (public API)
item.description: No secret key: the checkout token is the credential. This is the surface the hosted checkout page calls, so your own UI can render every rail itself - account numbers, wallet addresses with timers, QR codes, momo prompts - with no redirect.

request.description: Everything a checkout screen renders: amount, currency, payment_methods (with the currencies each corridor accepts), customer, success/cancel URLs.

exec: pm.test("session readable without an API key", () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.eql(200));

request.description: Buyer picked a number on your own UI: push it here before quoting. Only valid while the session price_type is custom and the amount sits inside minimum/maximum.
The API tells you which fields this rail needs next and names the endpoint to call. Bank transfer needs nothing, so next_step is get-quote.

item.name: 2b. Requirements: mobile money returns a network list

request.description: Momo is a two-step rail: pick the network (mtn / vodafone / ...) from this response, then quote with payment_rail. A second requirements call after the quote asks for the phone number.

item.name: 3. Quote: lock the rate and fee

request.description: Returns quote_id, the local amount, the processing fee and the exchange rate. Quotes are short-lived (minutes) - re-quote rather than retrying a stale one.
Returns payment_type=instructions with the real account name, number, bank, the amount expected and an expiry. polling_required tells you to watch /charges/{id}/status.

item.name: 4c. Complete: mobile money  ->  approve on phone

request.description: Phone must be +countrycode or 7-10 local digits. Returns instructions.action=approve_on_phone: render a prompt screen and poll.

Inline card rail. Returns payment_type=inline with a Stripe PaymentIntent client_secret: confirm it with Stripe.js/Elements in your own form. (This sandbox account settles USD cards through a processor instead - see the vault actions at the bottom for the direct path.)
Local card rail: no client_secret, payment_type=processing. The customer approves with the issuer (OTP / in-app) and you follow the charge status.
charge_status (open/paid/failed), substatus, attempt_status, failure_message/failure_code, redirect_url and amount_paid/amount_remaining. This is the state machine your UI renders.

item.name: 6. Mobile money: submit the approval code

request.description: Only when the network returns requires_otp rather than approve_on_phone. The sandbox prompt usually auto-approves, so this is a production path.

item.name: 7. Card: confirm with a token from elsewhere

request.description: Alternative to the vault: if you already minted a card token, hand it over here.

item.name: Card vault (direct card data)
item.description: The checkout page's own card path, callable from your server: card data sealed with the vault's public key, then Next.js server actions on the checkout origin. These action ids belong to a build - if Bachs redeploys the checkout, refresh them from the bundle. Prefer the inline Stripe rail when it is available.

request.description: Serve-side of the checkout origin. Import the SPKI PEM, encrypt an AES-256-GCM key with RSA-OAEP-SHA256, seal the card JSON. The SDK's CardVault.seal() does exactly this.
Mints a short-lived grant (120s) that authorises one tokenization. Body is the argument array. Response carries {grant, expires_in, collect_pin}.
Send the sealed card: {encrypted_key, iv, ciphertext} (base64). Returns a vault handle like vlt_... plus brand and last4. The PAN never appears in the response.
Fires the card payment. Then poll the public charge-status endpoint for the outcome.
Issuer asked for an OTP (next_action.type = requires_otp).
Some NGN cards require a PIN after tokenization (grant.collect_pin = true).

request.description:
Charge a customer's saved card off-session, meaning with nobody on a payment page. Use this for money a customer agreed to once and you collect later, such as a usage invoice or a top-up. An off-session charge cannot ask the customer to authenticate, so a card whose issuer demands it is refused.

The card must have been saved on an earlier checkout. See [Charge a saved card](/guides/payments/charge-a-saved-card).

This always answers with a payment, never an error, when the card is refused: a refusal is an outcome you read from `status`. The payment is usually `processing`, and the result reaches you as a `collection.succeeded` or `collection.failed` webhook. A card refused while the request is still open comes back already `failed`. A `201` is not payment received.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header. Without one, a retry after a timeout charges the customer twice.

request.description:
Update a destination: rename it, (de)promote it as a payout schedule's default, or restate where money lands.

`name` and `is_default` alone are safe: neither touches review status, since the default can only ever be one of your own approved destinations. Sending any routing detail (currency, type, account, wallet or phone) restates the destination in full, the same shape as `POST`; omitted routing fields fall back to what is already stored. Changing an account number, bank code, wallet, network, or phone number this way sends the destination back for review, because the approval it holds was granted for the details it is being asked to leave behind.

Common errors:
- `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`: neither `name` nor `is_default` sent, or an invalid payload for the destination type. Resolution: validate request fields and retry.
- `401 UNAUTHORIZED`: API key is missing, invalid, or revoked. Resolution: use a valid API key in the `Authorization` header.
- `404 NOT_FOUND`: `destination_id` was not found. Resolution: verify destination ID and retry.
